title: /login counts every signed-out visit: no source is a direct visit, and a linking site is kept as its host only
steps: S1: render the sign-in page with no source and with a source; read its visit script.

S2: POST /login/visit from the page's own origin with {ref:'x'}, {referrer:'www.google.com'}, {utm_source:'joomlart', referrer:'www.joomlart.com'} and {referrer:'www.google.com/search?q=secret'}; then with an array and a string body.
S3: visitReferrer with a host, a host with a path, a port, an at sign, a fragment and an empty string.
expect: S1: both pages send POST /login/visit once per tab; the page with no source sends {} and adds referrer only when document.referrer is another host.
S2: four login.visited rows {}, {referrer:'www.google.com'}, {source:'joomlart', referrer:'www.joomlart.com'}, {}; the array and string bodies keep nothing.
S3: the host cleaned to lower case; null for every value carrying anything past a host.
evidence: From 26/10 only visits from a link with utm_* were recorded, so direct, search and desktop-app visits to /login were invisible next to first sign-ins
fence: A visit row holds no account, address, cookie or path: the cleaned source values and a host at most, capped per client address

cmd: --test-name-pattern=tells /login/visit once per tab|visitReferrer keeps a cleaned host|POST /login/visit keeps
tests: the login page tells /login/visit once per tab
visitReferrer keeps a cleaned host and refuses anything past one
POST /login/visit keeps one cleaned source per visit
